# A stage can require the CALLER to declare something before it will start. The
# incident: a deploy convention ("take a pre-roll reading") written into a memory,
# then into AGENTS.md, and then broken twice in four hours by the person who wrote
# it. Two of three greens for one commit therefore rest on a binary nobody had a
# before/after for, and those readings cannot be retaken.
#
# The script-side version of this gate blocked EVERY deploy on the machine for half
# an hour, because a stage command inherits the DAEMON's environment — a variable
# exported in the operator's shell never reaches it, so the gate was unsatisfiable.
# Hence --set: the declaration travels with the trigger, not with a shell.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity admin
cp stdout admin.token
exec breeze register identity peri
cp stdout peri.token
exec breeze apply -f pipeline.hcl --as admin --token-file admin.token

# Legible before you trip over it, same as requires_lock: a status query has no
# caller, so it cannot answer "did they declare it" either.
exec breeze show pipeline guarded
stdout 'requires env: PREROLL_CONTROL'

# No declaration: refused, and the refusal says what is missing AND how to answer.
! exec breeze start stage guarded roll abc123 --as peri --token-file peri.token
stderr 'PREROLL_CONTROL'
stderr '--set'

# An empty declaration is not a declaration.
! exec breeze start stage guarded roll abc123 --set PREROLL_CONTROL= --as peri --token-file peri.token
stderr 'PREROLL_CONTROL'

# A real reading satisfies it.
exec breeze start stage guarded roll abc123 --set PREROLL_CONTROL=/tmp/before.txt --as peri --token-file peri.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# So does a DECLARED SKIP — breeze checks that you said something, never that it is
# any good. No script can know what a given change needs measured; the point is that
# "none" is something you type rather than something you drift into.
exec breeze start stage guarded roll def456 --set PREROLL_CONTROL='none: docs-only roll' --as peri --token-file peri.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# A name the stage never declared is REFUSED, not quietly ignored: these values land
# in the environment of a command the daemon runs.
! exec breeze start stage guarded roll aaa111 --set PREROLL_CONTROL=x --set LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/evil.so --as peri --token-file peri.token
stderr 'LD_PRELOAD'

# --set that is not NAME=VALUE is caught client-side, before anything is triggered.
! exec breeze start stage guarded roll bbb222 --set PREROLL_CONTROL --as peri --token-file peri.token
stderr 'NAME=VALUE'

# *** AND THE VALUE ACTUALLY REACHES THE COMMAND. *** A gate that forces a
# declaration the script cannot then read would be pure ceremony — the answer has to
# arrive at the thing that needs it. This stage exits 0 only if it does.
exec breeze start stage guarded consume ccc333 --set PREROLL_CONTROL=/tmp/before.txt --as peri --token-file peri.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# Inert for every pipeline written before this existed.
exec breeze start stage guarded plain abc123 --as peri --token-file peri.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# On an approval stage the value would reach nothing, so the config would claim a
# discipline it does not have. Refused where someone is looking at the file.
! exec breeze apply -f bad.hcl --as admin --token-file admin.token
stderr 'requires_env is not meaningful on an approval stage'

exec breeze stop

-- pipeline.hcl --
pipeline "guarded" {
  stage "roll" {
    type         = "command"
    requires_env = ["PREROLL_CONTROL"]
    timeout      = "10s"
    command      = ["/bin/true"]
  }
  stage "consume" {
    type         = "command"
    needs        = []
    requires_env = ["PREROLL_CONTROL"]
    timeout      = "10s"
    command      = ["/bin/sh", "-c", "test \"$PREROLL_CONTROL\" = /tmp/before.txt"]
  }
  stage "plain" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "10s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
  }
}

-- bad.hcl --
pipeline "wrong" {
  stage "review" {
    type               = "approval"
    required_approvals = 1
    approver_role      = "reviewer"
    requires_env       = ["PREROLL_CONTROL"]
  }
}
